summary: Root cause identified with high confidence (H1, 0.84): the infra-automation config change cfg-2207, which reduced portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 09:52:00Z, exhausted the service's datasource connection pool and surfaced as upstream timeouts/504s on /v1/portfolio/* at api-gateway. Minute-level data shows the discriminating causal ordering: the pool ran at 10.78–12.63 connections/min through 09:52Z, pinned at exactly 5.0 in the 09:53Z minute, and portfolio-service p99 broke from 172.69ms (09:52Z) to 4250.91ms (09:53Z) in that same minute, followed one minute later by HikariPool exhaustion logs (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43) and a 0.26%→22.3% error-rate step. The gateway's own HTTP/2 upgrade (08:00Z) is largely excluded: the gateway logs zero ERROR lines and zero http2/TLS protocol matches, its errors are pure upstream timeouts, request rate is flat, and order-service — which received the same h2 upstream change — shows zero errors on /v1/orders/*; all three of portfolio-service's downstreams and its own CPU are flat. Scope is confined to the one service whose pool was capped. Mitigation is to revert cfg-2207 (restore db.pool.max_size to 50) and confirm pool, p99 and 504 recovery; the change was never reverted in the data window, so the decisive recovery-on-revert signal is still untested.

ranked_hypotheses.title: portfolio-service datasource pool config (50→5) exhausted, gateway amplifies into 504s
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The infra-automation config change cfg-2207 applied to portfolio-service at 09:52:00Z ('Apply cost-optimisation profile small to service datasource') reduced db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5. The pool was consuming 10.8–12.6 connections per minute up to 09:52Z (F30), so capping it at 5 saturates demand immediately: db_pool_in_use pins at exactly 5.0 in the 09:53Z minute (F31), portfolio-service p99 breaks from 172.69ms in the 09:52Z minute to 4250.91ms in the 09:53Z minute (F32), and the first HikariPool exhaustion log (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43) appears at 09:54:29Z (F34). Requests that cannot acquire a JDBC connection within 3000ms fail (F11); service error_rate steps from ~0.26% to 22.3% one minute later (F33). api-gateway, fronting portfolio-service with an upstream timeout, converts the slow upstream into 504s on /v1/portfolio/holdings from 09:53:53Z (F8) and its p99/error rate step at 09:52–09:54Z (F29, F7). portfolio-service CPU (F13) and all three downstreams — ledger-db (F14), market-data-service (F15), redis-cache (F16) — remain flat, localizing the fault to portfolio-service's connection-pool configuration. Scope of the observed symptom is the /v1/portfolio/* path (F8, F11); /v1/accounts/* and /v1/orders/* show zero matching errors (F27, F28).

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2207 sets portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50→5 at 09:52:00Z (only change to portfolio-service in the window; no restart/redeploy accompanies it)
Pool demand is in baseline and well above the new cap immediately before the change: 10.78–12.63 connections/min through 09:52Z (11.89); no pre-saturation exists
In the 09:53Z minute the pool pins at exactly total=5; this is the first minute the cap binds
Same minute, portfolio-service p99 breaks from 172.69ms (09:52Z) to 4250.91ms (09:53Z) — no latency degradation exists before this point
Requests fail to acquire a JDBC connection within 3000ms; first HikariPool exhaustion log at 09:54:29Z with total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting up to 57
portfolio-service error_rate steps from baseline ~0.13–0.31% to ~22.3% at 09:54Z, one minute after the pool pin
api-gateway blocks on the slow upstream and emits upstream-timeout 504s on /v1/portfolio/holdings starting 09:53:53Z; gateway error_rate steps to 7.46% at 09:54Z and gateway p99 reaches ~4.3s
Failure stays confined to the portfolio path: zero /v1/accounts/* and /v1/orders/* error matches during onset, even though order-service also received the h2 upstream change
Downstreams are all healthy across onset, ruling out a shared-dependency origin for the slowness

assumptions: Normal portfolio-service concurrency genuinely needs more than 5 connections — supported by the observed 10.8–12.6 pre-change usage (F30), which makes saturating at 5 arithmetically inevitable

The pool cap is applied in place without a restart lag: no restart/redeploy event exists for portfolio-service (F19) and the binding is observed in the very next minute (F31/F32), so the change record timestamp is treated as the effective time
The change was never reverted in the data window (F20/F21), so no recovery-on-revert observation is available

ranked_hypotheses.title: api-gateway v9.3.0 HTTP/2 upgrade is a local regression in connection handling
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The gateway envoy upgrade at 08:00Z ('enable HTTP/2 to upstreams', envoy 1.29→1.30, h2 to portfolio-service and order-service) regressed the gateway's upstream connection handling, as in HIST-116 where an envoy upgrade changed the HTTP/2 max-concurrent-streams default and caused resets. Under this reading the new multiplexing stalls or over-subscribes streams to portfolio-service, raising upstream latency and yielding timeout 504s; portfolio-service's pool exhaustion is either a false lead or a downstream side-effect of altered concurrency.

causal_chain.claim: api-gateway v9.3.0 deployed 08:00Z with envoy 1.29→1.30 and h2 upstream protocol to portfolio-service and order-service
New HTTP/2 connection/stream handling on the gateway degrades or serializes upstream calls to portfolio-service
Gateway sees upstream timeouts and 504s on the portfolio path
Gateway p99 and error rate step up

assumptions: The envoy 1.30 upgrade introduces a stream/connection-handling regression analogous to HIST-116 (no surviving finding shows any such mechanism today)
The ~1h51m gap between deployment (08:00Z) and onset (09:51–09:53Z) is explained by gradual stream/connection accumulation — an explanation with no supporting signal in the data

ranked_hypotheses.title: Reporter's suspicion: gateway HTTP/2 change alters upstream concurrency, driving portfolio-service past its cap
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Directly addressing the on-call SRE's stated suspicion: the gateway's new HTTP/2-to-upstream behaviour could be the origin, with portfolio-service pool exhaustion appearing because the gateway's new connection semantics (e.g. more concurrent upstream requests per connection, or stream resets causing retries) multiply the demand on portfolio-service's datasource beyond its newly-capped pool. Under this reading the gateway rollout is the true origin and the 09:52Z pool config change is the proximate trigger that exposed it.

causal_chain.claim: Gateway v9.3.0 (HTTP/2 to upstreams) deployed 08:00Z
Gateway change alters upstream concurrency or retry behaviour toward portfolio-service, raising demand on its datasource
portfolio-service's 5-connection pool saturates and JDBC acquires time out
Gateway sees upstream timeouts → 504s and elevated p99

assumptions: The gateway's HTTP/2 change materially increased concurrent upstream demand on portfolio-service (no signal of this: gateway request rate is flat ~1200–1320 req/s, F9/F29)
Per-upstream concurrency could have changed even while aggregate request rate stayed flat — aggregate rate (F9) does not measure multiplexing, so this is not fully excluded by metrics alone

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared infrastructure / dependency failure behind the portfolio path
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A fault in a shared component on the /v1/portfolio/* path — ledger-db (shared by portfolio, order, payment) or redis-cache (shared by auth, portfolio, market-data) — degraded near 09:50Z and made portfolio-service slow, which the gateway then reported as 504s. Alternatively an exchange-gateway/external dependency degradation propagated upward through market-data-service.

causal_chain.claim: A shared component on the portfolio path degrades at ~09:50Z
portfolio-service blocks on that dependency, inflating p99
Gateway times out on the slow upstream → 504s

assumptions: Some shared or external component failed at onset despite flat metrics
The failure mode would still surface as local JDBC pool exhaustion with no corresponding upstream latency or error change
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Contradicted by flat, healthy metrics on every downstream: ledger-db slow_queries flat ~1/min with connections_active DROPPING ~61→~55 (F14); market-data-service p99 flat ~40ms and error rate flat (F15); redis-cache hit ratio steady ~96% (F16). The error signature is a local HikariPool exhaustion (F11, F34) that begins the exact minute the pool cap binds locally (F31, F32), with no dependency-side step change. A shared-dependency origin would also not be gated on a portfolio-service-only config change.

facts.statement: Two config changes occurred in the window; the only one touching portfolio-service is cfg-2207: db.pool.max_size old_value 50 → new_value 5 at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z, author infra-automation, description 'Apply cost-optimisation profile small to service datasource'.
portfolio-service db_pool_in_use was 10.78–12.63 connections per minute from 09:40Z through 09:52Z (11.89 at 09:52Z) — running well above the eventual cap of 5, with no pre-saturation queueing.
The pool cap first binds in the 09:53Z minute: db_pool_in_use drops to a pinned total=5 (avg 5.0, max 5) and stays exactly 5.0 for every subsequent minute through 10:10Z.
portfolio-service p99 was flat at 172.69ms in the 09:52Z minute and broke to 4250.91ms at 09:53Z — the same minute the pool pinned at 5; no degradation exists before 09:53Z.

portfolio-service's first error is at 09:53:19Z and its error signature is local JDBC connection-pool exhaustion: 270x 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' and 233x 'HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available ... (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43)', waiting depth up to 57.
The first HikariPool exhaustion log is at 09:54:29Z; no pool-wait/queueing log exists before 09:54Z.
portfolio-service error_rate was baseline ~0.13–0.31% through the 09:53Z minute (09:53 avg 0.26), then jumped to 22.3% at 09:54Z and stayed ~21–24%.

portfolio-service's own p99 was flat ~180ms through the 09:27Z bucket, then jumped to avg 3680.87ms in the 09:50Z bucket and held ~4130–4200ms through 11:45Z — the upstream service itself is slow, not just the gateway waiting on it.
api-gateway p99 was flat ~205–215ms through 09:48Z, then rose to avg 1606.91ms in the 09:51Z bucket and held ~4300–4440ms from 09:54Z onward.
api-gateway error_rate was flat ~0.2–0.29% in every 2-min bucket 09:40–09:52Z, then stepped to 7.46% at 09:54Z and held ~6.8–7.5%; request rate stayed flat ~1200–1320 req/s (no traffic surge).

The first gateway 504 on the portfolio path is at 09:53:53Z ('upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504'), accounting for 252 of 255 WARN lines in 08:00–12:00Z; the gateway's signature is upstream timeout, not connection refused or protocol error.
api-gateway logged ZERO ERROR-level lines in the full 08:00–12:00Z window, and log searches for 'http2' and TLS strings returned 0 matches (both non-truncated).

The only 'reset' matches on api-gateway in 08:00–12:00Z are 2 isolated WARN retry lines at 08:28:11Z and 11:11:55Z, straddling the onset with no cluster — no evidence of a connection-handling/HTTP2 regression.

Traffic on other gateway routes was unaffected during onset: /v1/accounts/* returned 0 matches and /v1/orders/* returned 0 matches for errors/timeouts/504s in 09:40–10:20Z, even though order-service also received the h2 upstream change.

All three services downstream of portfolio-service show flat, healthy metrics across onset: ledger-db slow_queries ~1.0/min with connections_active DROPPING ~61→~55 (F14); market-data-service p99 flat ~40ms and error rate flat ~0.2% (F15); redis-cache hit ratio steady ~96% (F16).
portfolio-service CPU was flat at 35–37% (mean 36.0%, max 39.78%) in every 9-minute bucket from 09:00Z through 11:51Z — not CPU-bound.

No restart/redeploy event exists for portfolio-service in 06:00–11:59Z (count 0); the only deployment anywhere in the window is api-gateway v9.3.0 at 08:00:00Z (envoy 1.29→1.30, h2 to portfolio-service and order-service).

cfg-2207 was NOT reverted in the data window: a query for 11:59Z→2026-03-11T06:00Z returned count 0 changes, and a narrow 09:50:00–09:53:30Z query for portfolio-service returned only cfg-2207 with no rollback entry; portfolio-service p99 and gateway 504s persisted to end of window.

portfolio-service exposes no dedicated db_pool_wait/queue-depth metric (available_metrics are only cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts), so queue depth was inferred from db_pool_in_use pinning plus the HikariPool 'waiting=' log field.

assumptions: Normal portfolio-service concurrency genuinely requires more than 5 JDBC connections; the observed 10.78–12.63 connections/min pre-change usage makes saturation at a cap of 5 arithmetically inevitable.

The pool cap took effect in place without a restart/reload lag: no restart or redeploy event exists for portfolio-service, and the binding is observed in the very next minute (09:53Z), so the cfg-2207 record timestamp is treated as the effective time.
No recovery-on-revert observation is available because cfg-2207 was never reverted within the data window; the decisive rollback experiment remains untested.
The absence of gateway-side HTTP/2/TLS/protocol error signatures is taken from non-truncated keyword and min_level=ERROR queries; it is not proof of absence in the one truncated gateway log fetch.

The remaining gaps (no exchange-gateway telemetry, unverified auth-service/user-service latency, no reload audit event, one-minute metric granularity) are secondary and do not change the conclusion, since the fault is localized to portfolio-service by the direct HikariPool exhaustion signature and the minute-level causal ordering.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) Saturation/queueing begins at 09:53Z, after the 09:52Z db.pool.max_size 50→5 change, and never precedes it — causal ordering that orders out an onset tied to the 08:00Z gateway deploy.

timeline.event: api-gateway v9.3.0 deployed ('Upgrade envoy filter chain; enable HTTP/2 to upstreams', envoy 1.29→1.30, h2 to portfolio-service and order-service); the only deployment anywhere in the incident window.
api-gateway error_rate still baseline ~0.21–0.32% per 20-min bucket; request rate flat ~1245–1280 req/s.
portfolio-service db_pool_in_use 12.63 connections/min — entirely in baseline and nowhere near any cap; no pre-saturation queueing.
api-gateway p99 first breaks from flat ~205–215ms to avg 1606.91ms (max 4418.76ms) in the 09:51Z bucket.

cfg-2207 applied to portfolio-service: db.pool.max_size 50→5, author infra-automation ('Apply cost-optimisation profile small to service datasource') — the only config change to portfolio-service in the window.
portfolio-service p99 still flat at 172.69ms in the 09:52Z minute; db_pool_in_use still 11.89 — no degradation before the cap binds.
api-gateway error_rate still flat ~0.2–0.29% in all 2-min buckets through 09:52Z.
Pool cap binds: db_pool_in_use drops to a pinned total=5.0 and stays exactly 5.0 every minute through 10:10Z; portfolio-service p99 breaks to 4250.91ms in the same minute.
portfolio-service's first error: 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' — 270 occurrences in window.
First api-gateway 504 on the portfolio path: 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504'.
api-gateway error_rate steps to 7.46% and holds ~6.8–7.5% through 10:20Z; portfolio-service error_rate jumps to 22.3% and holds ~21–24%.
First portfolio-service HikariPool exhaustion log: total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43 (waiting depth up to 57).
Incident INC-002 reported by on-call SRE: portfolio page timing out, gateway p99 through the roof, suspicion placed on the gateway upgrade.
Conditions persist to end of window: portfolio-service p99 ~4130–4200ms and gateway 504s ongoing; cfg-2207 never reverted, so no recovery-on-revert signal exists.

recommended_actions.action: Revert cfg-2207: restore portfolio-service db.pool.max_size to 50 (the pre-change value) and confirm the config service reports the new value applied.
recommended_actions.rationale: The pool cap 50→5 is the change that binds at 09:53Z and produces the local HikariPool exhaustion (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43) that drives the p99 break and the gateway's upstream-timeout 504s; restoring the prior value removes the saturation source. This also executes the decisive rollback experiment that was never run in the data window.

recommended_actions.action: After reverting, verify recovery in this order within 10 minutes: portfolio-service db_pool_in_use rises above 5 and stops pinning; portfolio-service p99 returns toward its ~180ms baseline; HikariPool waiting depth drops to 0 and 'could not acquire JDBC connection' errors cease; api-gateway 504s on /v1/portfolio/holdings stop and gateway error_rate falls back toward ~0.2%.
recommended_actions.rationale: Recovery-on-revert is the single strongest confirmation of H1 and was never observed because no revert occurred in the window; these are the exact signals that moved at onset and should move back.

recommended_actions.action: While the revert is in flight, do not roll back or restart api-gateway v9.3.0 and do not restart portfolio-service as a first step; if a restart is used at all, treat it only as a temporary measure and verify the pool value the running instance actually reads.
recommended_actions.rationale: Gateway-side evidence contradicts the HTTP/2 upgrade as the cause (zero gateway ERROR lines, zero http2/TLS matches, pure upstream-timeout signature, flat request rate, unaffected /v1/orders/* and /v1/accounts/*), so a gateway rollback would target the wrong component; a restart without reverting the config can restore service yet mask the true cause.

recommended_actions.action: Add a guardrail to the infra-automation cost-optimisation profile: for datasource sizing, require a floor tied to observed peak pool usage (e.g. never below the p99 of db_pool_in_use over the last 7 days, ~13 connections here) plus a capacity pre-check against the target service before applying 'small'.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-2207 set max_size to 5 against an observed steady-state demand of 10.78–12.63 connections/min, making saturation arithmetically inevitable; a demand-aware floor prevents the same class of change from being applied to any service.

recommended_actions.action: Add and alert on a datasource pool saturation signal for portfolio-service: expose a db_pool_wait/queue-depth metric (currently only db_pool_in_use exists) and page on db_pool_in_use >= 95% of max_size with HikariPool waiting > 0 for 2 consecutive minutes.
recommended_actions.rationale: There is no first-class queue-depth metric today, so queue depth had to be inferred from pool pinning and log lines; a direct saturation alert would have fired at ~09:53Z instead of relying on user reports at 10:05Z.

recommended_actions.action: Require canary/gradual rollout with automatic rollback for config changes that alter connection-pool or concurrency limits, and gate them behind a revert window (e.g. auto-revert if the target service's p99 or error rate degrades within 5 minutes of apply).
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-2207 was applied in place at 09:52Z, never reverted within the data window, and degraded portfolio-service within one minute; an automated revert within minutes would have capped the outage at ~3 minutes instead of >2 hours.

recommended_actions.action: Add route-level error/latency metrics (per-route error_rate and p99) to api-gateway and route-level alerting on upstream-timeout 504 rate, so failures on a single upstream path are detected and attributed without log archaeology.
recommended_actions.rationale: The gateway has no route dimension in its metrics, so the portfolio-specific blast radius was only establishable from log matching, and 252 of 255 WARN lines on one route had to serve as the detection signal.

recommended_actions.action: After mitigation, post-incident: reconcile incident-history HIST-115 ('datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile', resolved by reverting config) with today's cfg-2207 to confirm the duplicate failure mode and update the cost-optimisation runbook accordingly; examine whether HIST-116 (envoy HTTP/2 defaults) supplies any residual hardening we still want for the gateway rollout.
recommended_actions.rationale: HIST-115 matches today's mechanism almost exactly, indicating a recurrence that process controls should have caught; HIST-116 was the basis for the gateway suspicion, and although contradicted by today's evidence, confirming it was a correct non-cause closes the loop cleanly.

data_gaps: No revert of cfg-2207 was executed in the data window, so the decisive recovery-on-revert confirmation of H1 is still untested; the conclusion rests on onset-side causal ordering plus the direct exhaustion mechanism rather than on observed recovery.

There is no dedicated profile-apply/datasource-reload audit event or runtime reload confirmation, and no restart/uptime counter was queried for portfolio-service, so the exact sub-minute instant the new pool size took effect (and whether it applied in place or after a reload) is unverified; the binding minute 09:53Z is established only to one-minute granularity.
portfolio-service exposes no db_pool_wait/queue-depth metric, so queue depth was inferred from db_pool_in_use pinning plus the HikariPool 'waiting=' log field rather than measured directly.

No exchange-gateway or external-partner telemetry was reviewed, so a small residual contribution from the last hop behind market-data-service cannot be fully excluded — though market-data-service itself fronting it is flat and healthy.
auth-service and user-service latency were not queried, so whether the ~09:51Z onset is shared with other services (i.e. whether any broader infrastructure event coincided) is unconfirmed.

api-gateway has no route-dimension metrics and one gateway log fetch was truncated, so the 'no other route affected' and 'no protocol errors' claims rest on non-truncated keyword/min-level queries plus zero-match route log searches rather than a complete enumeration of all gateway log lines.

The gateway log fetch that returned 255 matches was truncated (40 returned), so absence of ERROR-level or lower-severity gateway lines is inferred from the separate non-truncated min_level=ERROR query, not from the truncated result itself.

ledger-db cpu/disk/replication_lag, redis-cache cpu/memory/evictions, and portfolio-service memory_pct/restarts were not queried; the already-checked CPU, DB slow-query/connection, and cache hit-ratio metrics support the localization but do not close these secondary dimensions.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Observing recovery (pool above 5, p99 back to ~180ms, HikariPool waiting 0, 504s ceasing) WITHOUT reverting cfg-2207 would falsify H1's mechanism as the sole cause and re-open the gateway/HTTP2 hypotheses.

Any evidence that portfolio-service's db_pool_in_use or p99 was already degraded before 09:52Z, or that saturation appeared prior to the config change, would break the min-ute-level causal ordering that underlies H1.

A surviving gateway-side signal at onset — e.g. non-truncated ERROR-level gateway logs, or http2/TLS/reset/protocol-error clusters, or connection refused/reset signatures on the portfolio upstream — would revive H2/H3 (the envoy 1.30 HTTP/2 change).

Evidence that the gateway's HTTP/2 change materially raised concurrent upstream demand on portfolio-service per connection (e.g. a per-upstream connection/stream concurrency metric stepping at 08:00Z) would support H3 even though aggregate request rate is flat.

A step change in ledger-db, market-data-service, redis-cache or exchange-gateway latency/errors at ~09:50–09:54Z would reopen H4 (shared-infrastructure/dependency failure) rather than a portfolio-service-local pool fault.

Discovery that cfg-2207 was never actually applied (e.g. no reload occurred, or the running instance still read max_size 50), or that a different concurrent change altered portfolio-service behavior, would invalidate H1's trigger attribution.

findings.statement: Only one code deployment occurred across ALL services in the incident window (06:00–11:59 on 2026-03-10): api-gateway v9.3.0 deployed at 08:00:00Z, 'Upgrade envoy filter chain; enable HTTP/2 to upstreams' (envoy 1.29→1.30, upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service), status 'live', rolled_back_at: null. No deployments at all in the 2026-03-09T00:00–2026-03-10T06:00 window.

Two config changes occurred in the window: order-service log.sampling_rate 0.1→0.2 at 07:00 (author config-bot, 'More request log sampling') and portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50→5 at 09:52 (author infra-automation, 'Apply cost-optimisation profile small to service datasource').

The portfolio-service db.pool.max_size reduction (50→5) at 09:52 is the change closest in time to the reported symptom onset (~10:05) and it targets a service directly in the /v1/portfolio/* path, whereas the reported suspect (gateway v9.3.0) landed at 08:00, ~2 hours earlier.

Dependency chain for /v1/portfolio/*: api-gateway → portfolio-service (http); portfolio-service depends downstream on ledger-db (db), market-data-service (http), redis-cache (cache); market-data-service depends on redis-cache (cache) and exchange-gateway (http). Shared components in this path: ledger-db ('shared":true') and redis-cache ('shared":true').

ledger-db is shared: it is reachable from portfolio-service (db), order-service (db) and payment-service (db), so a ledger-db problem can affect the portfolio path independently of api-gateway. redis-cache is shared by auth-service, portfolio-service and market-data-service.

Two historical precedents are direct leads, not evidence: HIST-116 (2025-12-18) 'HTTP/2 resets after gateway envoy upgrade' — 'Envoy upgrade changed HTTP/2 max concurrent streams default', resolved by rolling back the gateway; and HIST-115 (2025-09-25) 'order-service connection pool misconfiguration' — 'Datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile', resolved by reverting config. Both match the change types seen today.

findings.statement: api-gateway p99 latency was flat at ~205-215ms through the 09:48Z bucket, then jumped to avg 1606.91ms (max 4418.76ms) in the 09:51Z bucket and ~4300-4440ms from 09:54Z onward, holding ~4300ms through 11:45Z. The onset is therefore ~09:51-09:54Z, well before the 10:05Z report.

The first gateway 504 on the portfolio path is at 09:53:53Z: 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504'. That pattern accounts for 252 of the 255 WARN log lines in 08:00-12:00Z, all on /v1/portfolio/holdings -- the gateway's error signature is an UPSTREAM TIMEOUT, not connection refused or TLS/HTTP2 protocol errors.

api-gateway error_rate steps up at the same time: ~0.21% (max ~0.32%) every 20-min bucket from 06:00Z through 09:20Z, then avg 2.34% (max 7.74%) in the 09:40Z bucket and a sustained ~7.2% from 10:00Z onward. Request rate stayed flat (~1245-1280 req/s throughout), so this is not a traffic surge.

portfolio-service's own p99 was flat at ~180ms through the 09:27Z bucket, then jumped to avg 3680.87ms (max 4546.3ms) in the 09:50Z bucket and stayed ~4130-4200ms through 11:45Z. So the upstream service itself is slow, not just the gateway waiting on it.

portfolio-service's FIRST error is at 09:53:19Z and its error signature is database connection-pool exhaustion, not a network/protocol error: 270x 'GET /v1/portfolio/holdings failed: could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' and 233x 'HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 3000ms (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43)' with waiting depth up to 57. 503 of 505 matching lines in 08:00-12:00Z are ERROR level.

findings.verification_note: 2/3 refs verified (tc-015: quote not found in tool output)

findings.statement: portfolio-service db_pool_in_use was ~12 connections (max 13.3) through the 09:38Z bucket, then dropped to a pinned 5.0 from 10:06Z onward (the 09:52Z bucket averaged 5.49 with max 11.89). The pool is capped at 5 and saturated, which is consistent with the HikariPool 'total=5, active=5, idle=0' errors.

portfolio-service CPU is completely flat across the onset: avg 35-37% (mean 36.0%, max 39.78%) in every 9-minute bucket from 09:00Z through 11:51Z, so the service is not CPU-bound and its slowness is not a compute saturation problem.

ledger-db (shared postgres behind portfolio-service) shows no degradation at onset: slow_queries_per_min stayed at ~1.0/min (mean 1.03, max 1.62) with no step change through the whole 09:00-11:51Z window, and connections_active actually DROPPED from ~61-62 (avg 60.71 at 09:45Z) to ~54-55 (avg 54.4 at 09:54Z) and held there. If the DB were the bottleneck, we would expect slow queries or connection growth, not a drop.

market-data-service (portfolio-service's downstream HTTP dep via redis-cache -> exchange-gateway) is fully healthy across the onset: latency_p99 stayed flat at ~39-41ms (mean 40.02ms, max 43.82ms) and error_rate stayed flat at ~0.19-0.25% (mean 0.2%, max 0.32%) in every bucket from 09:00Z to 11:51Z -- no step change at ~09:50Z.

redis-cache (shared cache used by portfolio-service and market-data-service) is healthy: hit_ratio_pct held steady at ~96% (mean 96.09%, min 94.15%, max 98.06%) with no dip at the 09:54Z bucket or after.

The three services downstream of portfolio-service on the /v1/portfolio/* path (ledger-db, market-data-service, redis-cache) all show flat, healthy resource/health metrics across the onset window, while portfolio-service itself is the one with the pool-exhaustion errors and ~3.7-4.2s p99. This localizes the slow/hung behaviour to portfolio-service itself rather than its dependencies.

The only config change to portfolio-service in the entire investigation window is cfg-2207: key db.pool.max_size, old_value 50, new_value 5, changed_at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z, author infra-automation, description "Apply cost-optimisation profile 'small' to service datasource".

findings.statement: No service-restart / redeploy / restart-type event exists for portfolio-service to explain or delay apply: get_deployments(portfolio-service, 06:00-11:59Z) returned count 0 and scope "portfolio-service"; the only deployment anywhere in the window is api-gateway v9.3.0 (F1, 08:00Z).

No revert of the change after 09:52Z: a query for the window 11:59Z→2026-03-11T06:00Z returned count 0 changes, and a narrow query 09:50:00–09:53:30Z for portfolio-service returned only cfg-2207 with no rollback entry — so db.pool.max_size was NOT reverted in the data window.

Because no revert occurred, there is no recovery-on-revert signal to look for: portfolio-service p99 (~4130-4200ms) and gateway 504s persisted to end of window (per F10/F12 and F8), consistent with the change staying applied.

findings.statement: portfolio-service is not shared and has telemetry (has_telemetry true, shared false); its dependency edges confirm downstream ledger-db(db), market-data-service(http), redis-cache(cache) and upstream api-gateway(http), matching the /v1/portfolio/* path where the pool-exhaustion errors occur.

api-gateway produced ZERO ERROR-level log lines in the full 08:00-12:00Z window: query for min_level=ERROR returned total_matched 0, truncated=false, empty counts_by_level. The gateway only logs WARN for the incident; its error signature is not a gateway-side error/exception.

api-gateway log search for HTTP/2 protocol-error strings across 08:00-12:00Z returned 0 matches (total_matched 0, truncated=false), so there is NO logged 'http2' protocol error anywhere in the window.
api-gateway log search for TLS strings across 08:00-12:00Z returned 0 matches (total_matched 0, truncated=false) -- no TLS/handshake errors in the window.

The only non-truncated 'reset' matches on api-gateway in 08:00-12:00Z are 2 WARN lines, 'retrying idempotent request (attempt 2) after connection reset', at 08:28:11Z and 11:11:55Z. They are isolated (2 total), straddle the ~09:52Z onset (one 84 min BEFORE, one 80 min AFTER), and show no cluster at onset -- no evidence of a connection-handling/HTTP2 regression.

findings.statement: api-gateway log search for /v1/accounts/* in 09:40-10:20Z returned 0 matches (total_matched 0, truncated=false): NO errors, timeouts or 504s on the accounts route during onset.

api-gateway log search for /v1/orders/* in 09:40-10:20Z returned 0 matches (total_matched 0, truncated=false): NO errors, timeouts or 504s on the orders route during onset. Combined with the /v1/accounts/* result, the failure is confined to the /v1/portfolio/* path even though order-service also received the h2 upstream change.

api-gateway error_rate is flat at ~0.2-0.29% in every 2-min bucket 09:40-09:52Z, then steps to 7.46% at 09:54Z and holds ~6.8-7.5% through 10:20Z; request_rate stays flat ~1200-1320 req/s across the same buckets (no traffic surge). The error onset is ~09:52-09:54Z, i.e. coincident with the portfolio-service pool cap change at 09:52, not with the 08:00 gateway deploy.

Minute-level db_pool_in_use for portfolio-service is fully in baseline (never near cap) BEFORE 09:52Z: it ranges 10.78–12.63 connections per minute from 09:40Z (12.63) through 09:52Z (11.89). There is no queueing/pre-saturation; the pool was well above the eventual cap of 5, i.e. running under its former larger limit.

The pool cap first binds at the 09:53Z minute: db_pool_in_use drops to a pinned total=5 (avg 5.0, max 5) at 09:53Z and stays exactly 5.0 for every subsequent minute through 10:10Z. This is the exact minute saturation begins.

portfolio-service p99 is flat at ~172.69ms in the 09:52Z minute, then breaks to 4250.91ms at 09:53Z — the SAME minute the pool pins at 5. No latency degradation exists before 09:53Z (09:40–09:52Z range 172.69–191.43ms).

portfolio-service error_rate is baseline ~0.13–0.31% through the 09:53Z minute (09:53 avg 0.26), then jumps to 22.3% at 09:54Z and stays ~21–24% — the exhaustion symptom lags the 09:53Z pool pin by one minute.

The first portfolio-service HikariPool exhaustion log is at 09:54:29Z (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43) — i.e. no pool-wait/queueing log exists before 09:54Z, consistent with saturation starting at 09:53Z (just after the 09:52Z config change).

portfolio-service exposes no dedicated db_pool_wait/queue-depth metric (available_metrics are only cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts), so queue depth had to be inferred from db_pool_in_use pinning plus the HikariPool 'waiting=' log field.

Causal ordering: saturation/queueing begins at 09:53Z, AFTER the 09:52Z db.pool.max_size 50→5 config change — it does not precede 09:52Z. This confirms H1 (pool cap binds at 09:53Z, total=5) and orders out H2/H3, whose alternative onset (gateway 08:00Z deploy) is 2 hours earlier and would require pre-09:52Z saturation that the minute-level data does not show.
